summary: Nine comment-endorsed discoveries across developer tools, everyday apps, reading, and games.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories fully crawled | history + run artifact updated

items.name: PostHog
items.source_story_title: We've built an open-source feature flag server for 11 years
items.summary: Product analytics platform; a startup user praises its generous free tier.
items.why_included: Specific operational praise from a startup using it at roughly 5,000 monthly active users.
items.evidence: A startup user calls PostHog a backbone of the business and says the team has never paid for it.

evidence_sources.author: ceuk
evidence_sources.excerpt: We use it at a startup I'm involved in (~5k MAU) and we have never paid a penny which I am constantly surprised by since it's such a backbone for us.

items.name: First steps in bare-metal programming using UEFI
items.source_story_title: First steps in bare-metal programming using UEFI
items.summary: UEFI programming guide endorsed by a developer building a Zig bootloader.
items.why_included: A concrete learning resource with a first-hand account of practical use.
items.evidence: A developer praises the guide as a starting point and used it when building a Zig bootloader, while noting UEFI's sharp edges.

evidence_sources.author: edoceo
evidence_sources.excerpt: This guide is fantastic for getting rolling in the UEFI space. I used this as one of the references when building a bootloader with Zig. Has its own set of issue, especially that 16bit character situation.

items.name: Flynn
items.source_story_title: MoofTCP – A modern replacement for MacTCP on 68k Macs
items.summary: Telnet and Finger client for classic Macs, praised by a daily user.
items.why_included: An independently endorsed retro-computing tool discovered in a related networking thread.
items.evidence: A user thanks Flynn's creator, reports near-daily use, and credits it with inspiring 68k development patterns.

evidence_sources.author: marcusbasant
evidence_sources.excerpt: Thanks (again) for Flynn! I use it just about daily now, and it's been inspirational to my agents in developing patterns for 68k dev.

items.name: Photoflare
items.source_story_title: Blender's UI and Runtime: Much Faster Than GPUI
items.summary: Cross-platform image editor recommended for straightforward cropping, drawing, and small edits.
items.why_included: A direct usability recommendation answering a request for a simple Linux image editor.
items.evidence: A commenter answering a request for Paint-like editing calls Photoflare the most usable option they have found.

evidence_sources.author: graynk
evidence_sources.excerpt: https://photoflare.io/ is the one I've found to be most usable.

items.name: Metrolist
items.summary: YouTube Music client for Android, adopted as a replacement for Google's app.
items.why_included: A clear first-hand switch to a concrete alternative, not a neutral app mention.
items.evidence: A commenter says they uninstalled Google's music app and now use Metrolist exclusively.

evidence_sources.author: e12e
evidence_sources.excerpt: Ironically google music is so terrible I've uninstalled it and use Metrolist exclusively.

items.name: ING
items.source_story_title: Dutch 'idealist' bank ASN blocks non-Google Android, including GrapheneOS
items.summary: Banking app praised for working on one user's rooted LineageOS tablet.
items.why_included: Locally relevant first-hand compatibility praise, without generalizing to all devices or ING regions.
items.evidence: A user explicitly praises ING and reports full app functionality on a rooted custom-ROM tablet, with periodic security warnings.

evidence_sources.author: agilob
evidence_sources.excerpt: No other issues, it's not blocking me from doing anything, not forcing any updates, doesn't limit any functionality of the app.

items.name: Debt: The First 5,000 Years
items.source_story_title: From Linux to Wikipedia: How Volunteers Build the Internet
items.summary: David Graeber's history of debt, recommended against the familiar barter-origin story.
items.why_included: An explicit book recommendation emerging from a discussion of volunteer work and exchange.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends Graeber's book in response to a claim that barter preceded money.

evidence_sources.author: M95D
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend reading "Debt: The First 5,000 Years" by David Graeber.

items.name: How to Pave the Road to Hell
items.source_story_title: Britain to make salary disclosure in job ads mandatory
items.summary: Freakonomics podcast episode exploring salary transparency and its potentially unintended effects.
items.why_included: An explicitly praised episode adds research context to the salary-disclosure debate.
items.evidence: A commenter calls the Freakonomics episode good and notes that it features an author of the paper under discussion.

evidence_sources.author: trio8453
evidence_sources.excerpt: Freakonomics have a good episode including one of the authors of that paper

items.name: World Strike
items.source_story_title: Multiplayer tanks that demolish real buildings from OpenStreetMap
items.summary: Multiplayer browser tank game with destructible cities built from OpenStreetMap data.
items.why_included: An OpenStreetMap contributor explicitly loves the game while requesting better attribution placement.
items.evidence: An active OpenStreetMap contributor praises the game and asks its creator to improve the attribution placement.

evidence_sources.author: vfosnar
evidence_sources.excerpt: as an active osm contributor and community member and io games enjoyer i love this. if the author is readin this by any chance pretty please improve the attribution placement
